slides.title: Levenshtein Distance Created by Vladimir Levenshtein in 1965
slides.text: Levenshtein Distance Created by Vladimir Levenshtein in 1965 – Russian scientist who did research in information theory , error-correcting codes , and combinatorial design He graduated from the Department of Mathematics and Mechanics of Moscow State University in 1958 and worked at the Keldysh Institute of Applied Mathematics in Moscow ever since. He was a fellow of the IEEE Information Theory Society. a = string 1, b = string 2, i and j are the terminal character of string 1 and 2, respectively 1

slides.title: Jaro Similarity – Matthew a jaro It is
slides.text: Jaro Similarity – Matthew a jaro It is the minimum number of single-character transpositions required to change one word into another. Example – ‘ martha ’ and ‘ marhta ’; m=6, t=2/2=1,|s1|=6 and |s2|=6 dj = (1/3)*(6/6 + 6/6 + (6-1)/6)=(1/3)*(17/6)=.944 = 94.4% 2

slides.title: Jaro -Winkler Similarity – William e winkler 3
slides.text: Jaro -Winkler Similarity – William e winkler 3 From the previous example, ‘ martha ’ and ‘ marhta ’ dw = 0.944 + ( (0.1*3)(1-0.944) ) = 0.944 +0.3*0.056 = 0.961 = 96.1% Where p is a constant scaling factor, we use 0.1 here, which is the standard value and l is the length of common prefix at the start of the string (up to a max of 4 characters). So, l = 3.
